record.name: Guatemala
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. A UNDP-supported landscape assessment scored Guatemala 2.0 out of 5, and a national AI strategy is to be co-created in 2026 with UNDP, UNESCO and SENACYT.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. No retained English query. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English searches returned the government-led national strategy co-creation process and the AILA landscape assessment. The cached Commission GAE account organises work around the AI ecosystem, government use, regulation and ethics. Readiness/landscape assessment evaluates the national ecosystem rather than frontier models; no qualifying institute-specific proposal was found. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

related_bodies.name: Comision Presidencial de Gobierno Abierto y Electronico (GAE)
related_bodies.role: GAE's own account describes a multisector AI-policy dialogue with UNDP support and UNDP's presentation of the AI Landscape Assessment; no mandate to evaluate advanced models was identified in the retrieved material.

related_bodies.name: SENACYT
related_bodies.role: It leads AI strategy work as a science and technology secretariat. No evaluation mandate was found.

record.notes: The UN page (secondary) says regulation and governance are weak and a national strategy is to be co-created in 2026. A press report seen in search results gave a timetable (executive strategy in late November or December 2026; national policy in the first quarter of 2027, lead institution not decided); this is unverified and was not opened.
